videos.script: When a virtual machine runs, there are two operating systems on the computer. The host's, and the guest's. {{two}} They are more separate than people expect. Each has its own kernel, its own users, its own files and its own updates. Patching the host patches nothing inside a guest. {{separate}} But they are joined in a few places, and knowing those places is what lets you support both. A disk that is a file on one side. A network cable with one end on each side. {{joins}} The host can describe everything about a guest's hardware, because it invented that hardware. What happens inside the guest, it cannot see, unless the guest agrees to tell it. {{knows}} That agreement is a small program called the guest agent. You will ask it questions from the host, and then switch it off and watch the questions fail. {{agent}}
